result:
A quick flag before I draft this: "safe and fully backward compatible" is a strong, absolute claim, and self-run tests plus self-review are real evidence but fairly weak in isolation — especially for payment processing, where subtle backward-compat breaks (rounding, idempotency, serialization formats, webhook shapes) often slip past a generic test suite and a solo read-through. I'd rather write you an honest evidence table than a paragraph that overstates what you've actually verified — reviewers will trust it more, and it's more useful for them to know the gaps.

## Evidence

| Sub-claim | Status | Evidence | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing automated test suite passes against this diff | ✅ Verified (self-reported) | Full suite run locally by author, all green | Not yet confirmed on CI; local env may differ (config, dependency versions, DB state) |
| Diff has been reviewed for correctness | ⚠️ Partial | Line-by-line self-review completed | Self-review only — no independent reviewer yet; author blind spots aren't caught by definition |
| Refactor is backward compatible with existing callers/integrations | ❓ Unverified | None beyond passing existing tests | Existing suite may not target compat-sensitive behavior (API response shapes, error codes, idempotency, currency/rounding, webhook payloads) unless it was written for that purpose |
| Refactor is "safe" in production | ❓ Unverified | None | No staging run, canary, or shadow traffic comparison; "safe" implies more than test-suite pass |

**Suggested PR wording**, scoped to what's actually shown:

> This refactor passes the full existing test suite locally and has been self-reviewed line-by-line. It has not yet been reviewed by another engineer or run in CI/staging. Backward compatibility is asserted based on test coverage of [describe what the suite actually covers] — reviewers should confirm whether that coverage extends to [payment-critical paths you're unsure about, e.g., idempotency, currency handling, external webhook formats].

Two things worth doing before you post this, if you want the compat claim to actually hold up:
1. Push and let CI run — "I ran it locally" and "CI is green" aren't the same evidence.
2. Note explicitly whether the existing tests exercise the specific paths you touched, or just pass because they don't hit the changed code.

Want me to help identify which parts of the payment flow the current test suite actually covers, so you can either point to real coverage or flag the blind spots?
